text:
NASA ordered Boeing’s Starliner to return uncrewed from its first crewed flight because the spacecraft experienced five reaction-control system (RCS) thruster anomalies during the docking approach, and NASA determined that these anomalies could not be guaranteed safe for the deorbit burn since the thrusters could not be ground-tested in their flight condition [Source: ev-1].

This decision meant that astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams remained on the International Space Station until March 18, 2025, resulting in a stay of roughly 9.5 months compared to the planned ~8 days [Source: ev-1]. The program faced significant financial and operational setbacks under its fixed-price contract from the 2014 Commercial Crew program; Boeing disclosed cumulative losses of more than $1.5 billion by 2025 (against a total contract value of about $4.2 billion) and announced approximately 400 job cuts in its space division in June 2025 [Source: ev-1]. Furthermore, NASA’s certification path for Starliner remained unresolved through 2025 following the uncrewed return that landed at White Sands on September 7, 2024 [Source: ev-1].
